newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRIMEDIA SHARES TURNED ON BY ACQUISITION.
newsitem.headline: PRIMEDIA SHARES TURNED ON BY ACQUISITION.

text.p: Shares in Primedia Ltd jumped nearly six percent on Thursday on news that a bidding consortium of which it is part had won the licence to South African money-spinning radio station, Highveld Stereo.
The media and communication group's shares on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange climbed to a morning high of 17.80 rand, a jump of 5.9 percent from opening levels, in brisk trading.
By 1120 GMT shares had, however, slipped off their peaks to trade at 17.60, a gain of 80 cents after some 52,200 shares worth just under one million rand changed hands.
"The deal is positive for Primedia in terms of growth prospects and synergies," said a media analyst who asked not to be identified.
Primedia chief executive William Kirsh last month said his company would focus on building size by growing organically and by selective acquisition in a bid to dominate the media industry.

South Africa's Independent Broadcasting Authority announced on Wednesday that a consortium, Africa on Air (previously Newshelf 63), in which Primedia has a 40 percent stake, had secured the licence to the formerly state-owned Highveld.

The consortium, which includes Zerilda Investment, a black-owned investment company, is also in the running to buy Cape-based radio station KFM. The outcome of this bid will be known later on Thursday.
Analysts said the 320 million rand price tag paid for Highveld was a "fair" price.
In the year to June 30, 1996 Primedia posted a 34 percent rise in earnings to 50 cents per combined unit. Turnover surged 71 percent to 186.5 million rand.
